title: Goodwill: depreciation premise versus impairment risk
prompt: A colleague says: 'Goodwill is 45% of total assets, so depreciation expense will be high in the next 12 months.' Assess that premise and predict the risk of a material goodwill-related earnings charge during the prediction horizon. Use only the evidence below. Distinguish what is supported from what remains uncertain.

evidence.text: Reported goodwill is CU 4.5 billion, equal to 45% of total assets and 82% of book equity.
The group applies IFRS. Goodwill is not amortised; it is tested annually and when impairment indicators exist under IAS 36.
evidence.source: FY2024 annual report, significant accounting policies

evidence.text: The cash-generating unit holding 76% of goodwill recorded a 12% year-over-year revenue decline and a 430 basis point EBITDA-margin decline in FY2024.
Management's latest impairment test showed recoverable amount only 6% above carrying amount for that cash-generating unit.
A 50 basis point increase in the discount rate, with other assumptions unchanged, would eliminate the disclosed headroom.
The relevant five-year market yield increased by 35 basis points between management's impairment-test date and the case as-of date.

premise_check.description: A concise assessment of the colleague's accounting premise.

causal_factors.description: Short evidence-grounded factors supporting or weakening the prediction.

missing_evidence.description: Information that would materially change confidence.

rubric.description: Explicitly states that IFRS goodwill is not depreciated or amortised and that the relevant charge is impairment.
Does not treat a high goodwill balance by itself as proof that a future charge will occur.
Connects operating deterioration, limited headroom, rate sensitivity, and the observed yield move to elevated impairment risk.
Returns high risk without claiming that an impairment is certain or quantifying an unsupported charge amount.
Identifies material unknowns such as updated cash-flow forecasts, terminal growth, discount rate, allocation, or management actions.
